record.paper_title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces
record.original_question: If X is a consonant T0 space, is its Smyth power space PS(X) also consonant? Here consonance means that every Scott-open family of open subsets of X is generated by compact saturated subsets through the filters Phi(K)={U open: K subset U}.

evidence.quote: Question 6.15. ([5]) For a consonant T0 space X, is PS (X) also consonant?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a $T_0$ topological space, and let $\mathcal{O}(X)$ denote the lattice of open subsets of $X$. Recall that a family $\mathcal{H}\subseteq \mathcal{O}(X)$ is Scott-open if (i) it is an upper set (i.e., $U\in\mathcal{H}$ and $U\subseteq V\in\mathcal{O}(X)$ imply $V\in\mathcal{H}$) and (ii) whenever a directed family of open sets has union in $\mathcal{H}$, some member already lies in $\mathcal{H}$. For a compact saturated subset $K\subseteq X$ (saturated meaning $K$ equals the intersection of its open neighborhoods), define $\Phi(K)=\{U\in\mathcal{O}(X): K\subseteq U\}$. The space $X$ is called consonant if every Scott-open family $\mathcal{H}\subseteq \mathcal{O}(X)$ is a union of sets of the form $\Phi(K)$ for compact saturated $K\subseteq X$.

The Smyth power space $P_S(X)$ has underlying set the collection of all nonempty compact saturated subsets of $X$, equipped with the topology generated by the basic open sets $\square U=\{K\in P_S(X): K\subseteq U\}$ for $U\in\mathcal{O}(X)$.

Question: If $X$ is a consonant $T_0$ space, must the Smyth power space $P_S(X)$ also be consonant?
artifact.category_tag: Consonant spaces and Smyth power spaces
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in surveys on well-filtered and sober spaces in non-Hausdorff topology/domain theory. No published resolution was located; partial results address consonance under additional hypotheses, but the general implication "X consonant ⇒ P_S(X) consonant" appears to remain open.
